standard: strict modern real-time hero-character presentation, scored as a complete head rather than averaging prior local technical scores

rubric.evidence: The cranial vault is long and uniformly smooth; temple, zygomatic and mandibular plane changes remain weak in front, three-quarter and profile views.
The aperture exposes large triangular sclera wedges, lid margins lack physical thickness, lateral canthi read as holes and the gaze remains rigid under front and oblique inspection.
Lash density is technically present but the fan reads uniformly combed; pale sparse brows provide little anatomical framing.
Bridge-to-tip transition is generic; alar cartilage, nostril sill, nasolabial transition and cheek support remain under-defined across low, high and three-quarter views.
r1076 fixes the commissure normal spike, but vermilion volume, inner cavity depth, philtral columns and expressive compression remain shallow.
Broad highlights and near-uniform color make the face read as smooth synthetic material; pores, roughness zones and regional color variation do not survive full-head distance.
The center part exposes a wide bright scalp strip, the frontal boundary is hard and wig-like, and temple transitions lack short graded fibers.
The 72,800-point owned groom forms a straight uniform curtain with weak macro-clump hierarchy, limited silhouette breakup and repetitive lower ends.

rankedBlockers: eyes and eyelids: aperture, sclera wedges, lid thickness and canthus closure
hairline and scalp transition: wide bright part and hard frontal boundary
skin response: uniform color/roughness and broad synthetic highlight
nose/midface planes: weak alar, cheek and nasolabial structure
hair mass: straight curtain, weak clump hierarchy and repetitive ends
mouth/perioral: shallow vermilion, cavity and expression compression
